contract: One fixed telemetry event family [:elzoo, :job | :effect, :start | :stop | :exception] with declared integer measurements (queue_wait and duration in microseconds, payload_bytes as a byte count) and a metadata allowlist with positive per-key grammars (adapter, operation, request_ref as 64 lowercase hex, attempt 1..1_000_000, queue, tenant, outcome and reason as declared atoms) and required/optional keys per adapter operation. Elzoo.Telemetry.metadata/2 is the pure check; emit/4 calls :telemetry.execute/3 with only the clean subset, omitting failing keys in :production and raising ArgumentError naming only key names in :strict; emit/3 uses a compile-time default (:strict under Mix :dev/:test, else :production). Observation only.
limits: Not an audit record, usage meter, billing input or control receipt; an event may be missing. No exporter, aggregation, tracing, log format or persistence.

An opaque identifier-shaped secret passes the tenant grammar; secrets are kept out by the emission points' sources (named identity fields only), the grammar is a second layer. A host that names a tenant or queue with a secret is outside this Contract.

Handlers run synchronously in the emitting process (telemetry): a handler's run time is elapsed time; a handler slower than the remaining deadline makes the operation expire exactly as any other delay would. Handlers must be fast and non-blocking; offload work.
The allowlist and unit table are finite data checked by tests; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios: the README event, unit, key, operation and outcome tables equal Elzoo.Telemetry.schema/0; a short valid publication JSON, a 4 KiB binary, URLs with and without credentials, Bearer/Basic header values, base64, control bytes, non-ASCII, maps, lists, an Oban job and an exception struct fail every string grammar; unknown keys (authorization, token, payload, url, error) are refused; identifier-shaped secrets pass the tenant grammar (stated limit); strict mode raises naming key names only, production mode omits and still emits; invalid measurements; unknown event names are never emitted; raising, throwing and exiting handlers are detached by telemetry after their first failure while a healthy handler keeps receiving; an absent handler is silent. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

telemetry 1.4.2 synchronous execute/3 in the calling process, attach/attach_many/detach, detach of a handler that fails and the [:telemetry, :handler, :failure] event are upstream contracts, named and exercised in the listed scenarios, not proved.
OTP 29.1.2 :crypto SHA-256 and erlang:monotonic_time are upstream contracts.
Elixir 1.20.4 Regex, DateTime.diff and System.convert_time_unit are upstream contracts.

telemetry.contract: This Piece is the event family: fixed names, integer measurements with declared units, positive-grammar metadata allowlist, strict/production modes; handlers synchronous, may be absent, a failing handler is detached by telemetry.

config.contract: The allowlist and units are fixed data; the mode is a compile-time build property, not a runtime setting.

control.contract: No lifecycle or control surface; emission is a function call.
